subject: How to trigger drawing of initially hidden plots?

messages.author: 682090cd21a95bdb
messages.subject: How to trigger drawing of initially hidden plots?
parts:
I am having a problem with plots that are initially "hidden" (style=display:none).

If I try to change the display property from "none" to "block", the plot will not get drawn (unless it is initially set to "block").

I created some code below that I believe is the essence of the problem I am having.

working version:
library(shiny)
ui <- fluidPage(
  tags$button(
    id = "button",
    "button"
  ),
  tags$div(
    id = "plot_div",
    style = "display:block",
    plotOutput("mtcarsPlot")
  ),
  tags$script(
    '
    $(document).ready(function () {
      $("#button").on("click", function () {
        alert("button clicked");
        $("#plot_div").css("display", "block");
      });
    })
    '
  )
)
server <- function(input, output) {
  output$mtcarsPlot <- renderPlot({
    plot(mtcars$mpg,
         mtcars$cyl)
  })
}
shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)

not working version:
library(shiny)
ui <- fluidPage(
  tags$button(
    id = "button",
    "button"
  ),
  tags$div(
    id = "plot_div",
    style = "display:none",
    plotOutput("mtcarsPlot")
  ),
  tags$script(
    '
    $(document).ready(function () {
      $("#button").on("click", function () {
        alert("button clicked");
        $("#plot_div").css("display", "block");
      });
    })
    '
  )
)
server <- function(input, output) {
  output$mtcarsPlot <- renderPlot({
    plot(mtcars$mpg,
         mtcars$cyl)
  })
}
shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)


My question is: Why does setting the display property to "block" (via jQuery) not cause the plot to be drawn?

Also, is there another way to force the plot to be drawn?

Thank you,
Eric

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: How to trigger drawing of initially hidden plots?
parts:
to this:

$("#plot_div").show().trigger("shown")

It's the trigger("shown") (and trigger("hidden") when you're hiding) that tells Shiny to look at whether any outputs have been hidden or revealed.

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: How to trigger drawing of initially hidden plots?
parts:
(Sorry, your messages keep getting caught by Google Groups' spam filter, despite me whitelisting you.)

1) Your template.html is loading a copy of jQuery, which Shiny is also doing. If you load two copies of jQuery, bad things happen; please remove the script tag you're using for jQuery and just let Shiny load its copy.

2) You need to add this to your <head>:

    <script>
        $(document).on("click", "li.tab a", function() {
            $(this).trigger("shown");
        });
    </script>

With these two changes, it works for me.

On Fri, Apr 7, 2017 at 4:31 PM EA <eric.ray...@gmail.com> wrote:
Thank you for the quick response. The solution you provided works for the example. However, in my example, I think I oversimplified the problem and this solution did not solve my situation.

The bigger picture of what I am trying to do is use the materialize framework (materializecss.com) with shiny. The issue I am running into is with using tabs.

The same general problem arises, in which if a plot is not on a tab that is initially "active" (being displayed), the plot will never render, even when selecting the tab.

I have provided a simple example below that contains the issue I am experiencing. I used an htmlTemplate as my ui.

app.R
library(shiny)

ui <- htmlTemplate(
  filename = "template.html",
  mtcarsPlot1 = plotOutput('mtCarsPlot1'),
  mtcarsPlot2 = plotOutput('mtCarsPlot2')

)

server <- function(input, output) {

output$mtCarsPlot1 <- renderPlot({
    plot(mtcars$mpg,
         mtcars$cyl)
  })
  output$mtCarsPlot2 <- renderPlot({
    plot(mtcars$cyl,
         mtcars$hp)

})
}

shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)

template.html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
<head>
    {{ headContent() }}
    <!-- Compiled and minified CSS -->
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/materialize/0.98.1/css/materialize.min.css">
</head>
<body>
    <div class="row">
        <div class="col s12">
            <ul class="tabs">
                <li class="tab col s3"><a href="#tab1" class="active">Tab 1</a></li>
                <li class="tab col s3"><a href="#tab2">Tab 2</a></li>
            </ul>
        </div>
        <div id="tab1" class="col s12">
            {{ mtcarsPlot1 }}
        </div>
        <div id="tab2" class="col s12">
            {{ mtcarsPlot2 }}
        </div>
    </div>
    <!--Import jQuery before materialize.js-->
    <script type="text/javascript" src="https://code.jquery.com/jquery-2.1.1.min.js"></script>
    <!-- Compiled and minified JavaScript -->
    <script src="https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/materialize/0.98.1/js/materialize.min.js"></script>
</body>
</html>

The issue in the app above is that mtcarsPlot2 will never be displayed.

Thank you for the help, 
Eric

Try changing this line:

$("#plot_div").css("display", "block")

to this:

$("#plot_div").show().trigger("shown")

It's the trigger("shown") (and trigger("hidden") when you're hiding) that tells Shiny to look at whether any outputs have been hidden or revealed.
